original_abstract.text: When a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model does not fit in GPU memory, batch-1 decoding is dominated by copying expert weights from host memory. Cache-aware routing reduces these copies by biasing the router toward resident experts, but combined with asynchronous prefetching it makes the model's outputs depend on transfer timing, so a harness that does not simulate that timing no longer evaluates the deployed model. We propose prefetch-steered routing (PSR): routing conditions on a deterministic logical cache, into which at most n experts predicted by the next layer's router are inserted per layer and token; physical copies affect only latency. On OLMoE-1B-7B with 50% and 25% of experts resident on an RTX 4090, PSR decodes 2.2-2.3x faster than exact routing with LRU and 25-30% faster than the Cache-Prior operating point, with mean benchmark differences of +0.1 and +0.5 points (95% lower bounds -0.8 and -0.3). In greedy generation its lead over Cache-Prior depends on the workload and reverses on HumanEval at 50% residency. On Moonlight-16B-A3B, PSR is 1.9x faster than exact routing with LRU at 37.5% residency and, at the latency of Cache-Prior, significantly better on three of eight benchmarks. On Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, where copies are cheap relative to computation, PSR keeps its advantage over Cache-Prior on the likelihood benchmarks but not its speed. Distillation-trained gates did not help. Speculative decoding with block-level expert selection was slower than PSR with a 1B autoregressive drafter on OLMoE, but with a block drafter on Qwen3.6 it was 2.1-2.9x faster than any autoregressive configuration with at most its GPU memory on the 64 prompts we timed.
original_abstract.source_title: Prefetch-Steered Routing: Deterministic Cache-Aware Expert Selection for Offloaded Mixture-of-Experts Decoding

en.text: Uses a deterministic logical expert cache to steer routing in offloaded MoE decoding, separating model decisions from physical transfer timing. Reported speed and quality tradeoffs vary by model, expert residency and workload; results provide a reproducible way to study cache-aware routing and prefetching together.

zh.text: 用确定性的逻辑专家缓存决定路由，让实际拷贝时序只影响延迟，避免异步预取改变模型输出。多模型实验比较专家驻留比例、速度和任务表现，为专家卸载、缓存感知路由与预取的联合评估提供可复现设计。

original_abstract.text: Generative retrieval (GR) typically relies on item-level beam search to retrieve candidates, leaving cross-item dependencies unmodeled and limiting direct optimization of list-level objectives. A natural alternative is to generate the entire list within a single autoregressive trajectory. However, greedy decoding with directly trained list-wise models substantially underperforms beam search. We identify two contributing factors: the broader search space explored by beam search and the positional bias of scarce positive signals, which deprives later positions of adequate supervision. To address these challenges, we propose $\textbf{SLIDE}$, a search-to-list item distillation framework that decouples offline search from online list generation. A teacher model retrieves high-quality candidates through offline item-level beam search, providing additional conversion-relevant supervision beyond sparse behavioral labels. Their Semantic IDs (SIDs) are then concatenated in beam-score order to form list-wise distillation targets. This search-to-list conversion transforms candidates retrieved along separate search paths into sequential item-generation targets within a single trajectory. Trained on these targets, the student generates the Top-$K$ list in a single greedy pass, also decoupling teacher scaling from online deployment. Experiments on FORGE and Taobao Search show that SLIDE substantially improves retrieval quality under single greedy decoding and, with stronger offline teachers, surpasses the beam-search reference. Supplementary RL experiments support the effectiveness of list-level generation.
original_abstract.source_title: SLIDE: Search-to-List Item Distillation for Single-Rollout Generative Retrieval

en.text: SLIDE addresses weak greedy list generation by distilling offline item-level beam search into a single online trajectory. Teacher candidates are ordered by beam score and their semantic IDs concatenated as list-wise targets. On FORGE and Taobao Search, this improves single-pass retrieval, and stronger offline teachers exceed the beam-search reference. It separates teacher scaling from online deployment without claiming measured production speedups.

zh.text: SLIDE 针对贪心列表生成效果不足，将离线逐商品束搜索蒸馏到单条在线轨迹：按束分数排列教师候选，并将语义 ID 拼接成列表监督目标。在 FORGE 和淘宝搜索上，它改善了单次贪心检索；更强的离线教师还能超过束搜索参考。该方法将教师扩展与在线部署分开，摘要未报告实测生产加速。

original_abstract.text: Effective discrete representation learning with VQ-VAE serves as a fundamental component of modern autoregressive generative models. However, it is widely known to suffer from codebook collapse and inefficient code utilization. To address this issue, we propose FlowVQ, a simple yet effective alternative to standard vector quantization by formulating neural quantization as a joint modeling and clustering process. Specifically, we learn the latent space using a lightweight flow matching model alongside training, corresponding to a probability flow ODE that transports an often fixed well-behaved source distribution while preserving probability mass. Based on this, we define the codebook C_1 by transporting even-quantile partitioned prior codes C_0 from the source space through the learned flow, and obtaining the Voronoi centroids under the induced distribution, leading to a structured discretization. We evaluated on image tokenization and generation, as well as on two tasks requiring high-precision tokenization, demonstrating scalability and improved expressivity of the codebook with full utilization.
original_abstract.source_title: Transporting Quantiles to Codebook: Scalable Vector Quantization without Codebook Collapse

en.text: FlowVQ tackles VQ-VAE codebook collapse by jointly learning a latent distribution with a lightweight flow-matching model and constructing codes from equal-quantile partitions transported through that flow. Voronoi centroids provide the resulting structured discretization. Image tokenization/generation and two high-precision tokenization tasks show scalable, expressive codebooks with full utilization; recommendation semantic IDs remain a potential application rather than an evaluated result.

zh.text: FlowVQ针对VQ-VAE码本坍塌，将轻量流匹配学习与量化结合：把源分布等分位划分得到的初始码通过概率流搬运，再构造Voronoi质心形成结构化码本。图像token化、生成和两项高精度token化任务显示其可扩展性、表达能力与完整码本利用率；推荐语义ID属于可借鉴方向，尚非论文已验证的结果。

original_abstract.text: Generative recommendation with semantic IDs (SIDs) represents each item as a sequence of discrete tokens and autoregressively predicts the next item's SID. Despite strong recommendation performance, repeated decoding over multiple SID positions incurs substantial inference cost. Knowledge distillation transfers knowledge from a powerful generative teacher to a lightweight student, yet conventional objectives do not fully account for multi-token SID generation. We identify two limitations: item-level distribution alignment may not adequately preserve the teacher's ranking of candidate groups sharing SID prefixes, while uniform alignment across SID positions may affect final item ranking differently. We propose MuSID-KD, which combines Hierarchical Candidate Distribution Alignment (HCDA) and Ranking Impact Guided Levelwise Distillation (RIGD). HCDA aggregates item probabilities according to shared SID prefixes and aligns candidate distributions at successive levels, from candidate groups to individual items. RIGD evaluates the reduction in pairwise ranking surrogate loss when one student score contribution is replaced with the teacher's contribution, and allocates supervision accordingly. Experiments on real-world recommendation datasets using three lightweight student architectures demonstrate improved recommendation accuracy and better alignment of prefix marginal distributions and pairwise item rankings, without modifying the student's online inference architecture. Code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/m7k2-review-83f9/.
original_abstract.source_title: MuSID-KD: Multigranularity Knowledge Distillation for Generative Recommendation with Semantic IDs

en.text: MuSID-KD transfers semantic-ID recommendation knowledge to lightweight students at multiple granularities. It aligns candidate distributions aggregated by shared prefixes and allocates token-level supervision according to estimated ranking impact. Experiments with three student architectures report better recommendation accuracy and closer prefix and pairwise ranking alignment without changing online inference architecture. This is a training-side method for preserving ranking quality in compact generative recommenders.

zh.text: MuSID-KD 在多个粒度上向轻量学生模型蒸馏语义标识符推荐知识。它按共享前缀聚合并对齐候选分布，再依据估计的排序影响分配各令牌位置的监督。三类学生架构的实验报告了推荐准确率、前缀分布和物品两两排序对齐的改善，在线推理架构保持不变。其价值是在训练阶段帮助紧凑生成式推荐模型保留排序质量。

original_abstract.text: Navigational search aims to find a single target page among hundreds of millions of web pages. Click tables work well for queries seen before but cannot generalise to new formulations, while embedding retrievers generalise across content but often rank navigational targets poorly. We introduce Octen-WebGR, a generative retrieval framework that stores web pages in the parameters of a language model: given a query, the model generates a two-token semantic identifier constrained to a table of real URLs. We develop Octen-WebGR-4B, which indexes 201 million web pages, and evaluate it on real navigational traffic from the month after training. Generative retrieval is most effective on new ways of asking for familiar pages: for unseen queries targeting pages with substantial interaction history, it ranks the correct page first 30.9% of the time, against 17.2% for a dense retriever trained on the same clicks (21.4% with a click prior). Embedding retrieval keeps an advantage on rarely visited pages, so the two approaches generalise on complementary sides, the query and the page. Over all navigational traffic, Octen-WebGR reaches 59.6% top-1 accuracy, against 46.5% for a click-enhanced dense retriever and up to 37.5% for frontier LLMs answering from memory, which cost at least 40 times as much per query. The 4B model runs on a single GPU with 10 GB of memory, compared with 412 GB for exact dense retrieval. Scaling experiments with up to 32 million URLs show that, when every query-page pair is seen equally often, the model size needed grows sublinearly with index size, and that retrieval is constrained more by page exposure than by model capacity. We release Octen-WebGR-4B and Octen-WebGR-0.6B with their identifier tables and inference code.
original_abstract.source_title: Octen-WebGR: Scaling Generative Retrieval to 200 Million Web Pages

en.text: Octen-WebGR retrieves web pages by generating a two-token semantic identifier constrained to real URLs. Its 4B model indexes 201 million pages and reaches 59.6% top-1 accuracy on subsequent navigational traffic, versus 46.5% for a click-enhanced dense retriever. It is strongest on new queries for well-exposed pages; dense retrieval retains an advantage on rarely visited pages. Experiments up to 32 million URLs link capacity requirements to index size and exposure, offering evidence for large-scale generative retrieval rather than CTR ranking.

zh.text: Octen-WebGR 生成受真实 URL 表约束的双令牌语义标识符来检索网页。其 4B 模型索引 2.01 亿网页，在训练后月份的导航搜索流量上取得 59.6% 的首位命中率，结合点击先验的稠密检索为 46.5%。优势主要来自熟悉网页的新查询，稠密检索在少访问网页上仍有优势。最多 3200 万 URL 的缩放实验分析了索引规模、曝光与容量需求，可参考于大规模生成式检索，尚非 CTR 排序验证。

original_abstract.text: Large-scale industrial ranking models must jointly capture heterogeneous feature interactions, long-term user behaviors, and multi-scenario dependencies under stringent online serving constraints. Existing architectures typically process sequential and non-sequential features with separate modules, limiting bidirectional information exchange. Directly applying homogeneous self-attention to all semantic tokens can also be inefficient when sequential and non-sequential signals exhibit different effective-ranks (eRanks). Meanwhile, shared representations can overlook scenario-specific patterns and induce negative transfer between scenarios. In this paper, we propose HiRank, a unified framework for multi-scenario recommendation that jointly models Heterogeneous feature Interactions via effective-Rank scaling. HiRank integrates gated sequential attention with heterogeneous feature interaction within a unified backbone, enabling bidirectional fusion between sequential and non-sequential representations. HiRank further uses scenario-aware aggregation to compress heterogeneous low-order tokens into a compact representation. Distinct learned projections transform the full compact representation into scenario-aware composite tokens with complementary global feature views and more uniform information density, enabling more effective high-order self-attention. Extensive experiments on industrial-scale datasets demonstrate favorable performance scaling with parameter count and consistent improvements over competitive baselines. Online A/B tests further show a 2.27% increase in orders per user.
original_abstract.source_title: Unified Heterogeneous Feature Interaction via Effective-Rank Scaling for Recommender Systems

en.text: HiRank addresses industrial ranking with heterogeneous features, long user histories and multiple scenarios. A unified backbone combines gated sequence attention with bidirectional feature interaction, then compresses low-order tokens into scenario-aware composite tokens for high-order attention. Industrial experiments report favorable parameter scaling and an online 2.27% increase in orders per user. The contribution is unified ranking architecture rather than a general scaling law.

zh.text: HiRank 面向同时包含异构特征、长行为历史和多场景的工业排序。它在统一骨干中结合门控序列注意力与双向特征交互，再将低阶令牌压缩为场景感知的组合令牌，用于高阶注意力。工业实验显示随参数增长的效果改善，线上 A/B 测试报告人均订单量提升 2.27%。主要贡献是统一排序架构，而非通用缩放定律。

original_abstract.text: Large language models incur substantial training and inference costs in personalized search and recommendation, as growing interaction histories lengthen request inputs and repeatedly expose the same item text to the model. We propose \textbf{C}omposable and \textbf{R}eusable \textbf{I}tem \textbf{M}emory (CRIM), a framework that separates item-level semantic encoding from request-level history modeling. A small set of learnable summary tokens compresses each item into compact continuous memories, while segment-level readout tokens (REC tokens) introduce predictive supervision within the interaction history. These memories are independent of users and queries and can therefore be reused across requests. At inference time, CRIM composes cached memories in interaction order and incorporates an optional query to produce a personalized retrieval representation, reducing repeated item-text encoding while retaining request-dependent contextual modeling. We further introduce a joint training mechanism that combines cached memories with sampled live re-encoding. Re-encoding only a few history items per request allows the retrieval objective to jointly optimize the item and request encoders at limited computational cost, while periodic cache refreshes maintain consistency. Extensive evaluation and cost analysis on MovieLens-1M, Qilin, and our new LazSeq dataset show that CRIM achieves state-of-the-art retrieval performance with substantially lower inference costs at the same backbone scale, while limiting item re-encoding during joint training. We will publicly release our code and dataset.
original_abstract.source_title: CRIM: Composable and Reusable Item Memory for Efficient Personalized Retrieval

en.text: CRIM reduces repeated item-text encoding in personalized retrieval by compressing each item into user- and query-independent continuous memories. Requests compose cached memories in interaction order, while readout tokens and sampled live re-encoding support joint training with periodic cache refreshes. Evaluations on MovieLens-1M, Qilin and LazSeq report stronger retrieval with lower inference costs at the same backbone scale. The reusable item representation offers a practical route to compressing recommendation histories without removing request-level context modeling.

zh.text: CRIM 将物品压缩为不依赖用户和查询的连续记忆，减少个性化检索中重复编码物品文本的开销。请求按行为顺序组合缓存记忆，训练通过读出令牌、少量物品实时重编码和定期缓存刷新共同优化编码器。在 MovieLens-1M、Qilin 和 LazSeq 上，同等骨干规模下报告了更好的检索效果和更低推理开销。可复用物品表示为历史压缩提供了工程方案，同时保留请求层面的上下文建模。

original_abstract.text: Looped Transformers offer a parameter-efficient approach to language modeling by repeatedly applying a shared backbone. Vanilla looped Transformers use each backbone output directly as the input to the next iteration. These outputs may contain information useful several iterations later, but retaining it across the loop depends entirely on the single hidden state. We introduce StateLoop, which maintains one additional persistent state per token to retain information across iterations. At each iteration, a learned gate controls how much of the previous state is retained and how much information from the backbone output is incorporated. The updated state is projected back and added to the backbone output for subsequent iterations and final prediction. This design reduces Pile perplexity and improves average accuracy across eight zero-shot tasks over Vanilla Looped. Its perplexity advantage over Vanilla Looped grows with trained loop depth, consistent with persistent state becoming increasingly useful as recurrent computation deepens.
original_abstract.source_title: StateLoop: Persistent State for Looped Transformers

en.text: StateLoop adds a persistent state to every token in a looped Transformer. A learned gate retains and updates information across iterations, and a projection feeds that state back into subsequent computation and prediction. It lowers Pile perplexity and improves average accuracy across eight zero-shot tasks against vanilla looping, with the perplexity advantage growing at greater trained depth. The mechanism is relevant to parameter-sharing architectures, but transfer to ranking remains untested.

zh.text: StateLoop 为循环 Transformer 的每个令牌增加持久状态，通过可学习门控在迭代间保留和更新信息，再将该状态投影回后续计算与预测。相对普通循环，它降低了 Pile 困惑度并提高八项零样本任务的平均准确率，且困惑度优势随训练循环深度增加而扩大。该机制可供参数共享架构参考，迁移到排序仍待验证。

original_abstract.text: Cross-domain sequential recommendation aims to improve next-item prediction in a target domain by leveraging user behavior from auxiliary source domains. However, real-world deployment faces two critical challenges: business constraints that isolate interaction data across domains, and user heterogeneity, where many users lack cross-domain activity. This makes existing cross-domain methods difficult to apply. In this paper, we propose a simple and practical framework for cross-domain sequential recommendations that transfers information exclusively through learned user representations, without sharing raw interaction data or item embeddings across domains. We introduce a lightweight adapter that projects the source-domain user representation into the target-domain embedding space and integrates it with the target interaction sequence. Importantly, when source data is unavailable (i.e., the user observed only in the target domain), the model seamlessly defaults to a robust target-only sequential recommender, retaining benefits from joint training across all users. Extensive experiments were conducted under two setups; one targets benchmarking against previous baselines, while the other focuses on realistic and scalable conditions. Both sets of experiments demonstrate consistent performance gains for shared and unshared users.
original_abstract.source_title: Cross-Domain Sequential Recommendation with Representation-Level User Transfer

en.text: Transfers cross-domain information through learned user representations and a lightweight adapter, without sharing raw interactions or item embeddings. Shared and target-only users are trained jointly, with target-only fallback when source representations are unavailable; experiments cover benchmark and deployment-oriented settings.

zh.text: 跨域迁移仅交换用户表征，通过轻量适配器接入目标域序列，减少对原始行为和物品嵌入共享的依赖。源域信息缺失时回退为目标域模型，实验同时覆盖跨域活跃用户与单域用户，为受业务隔离约束的序列推荐提供实现思路。

original_abstract.text: Looped Transformers increase computation per token by repeatedly applying a shared backbone, offering a way to improve language modeling and downstream task performance at a fixed backbone parameter count. However, each loop depends on the preceding loop, so increasing recurrent depth also increases decoding latency. Existing approaches include Parallel Loop Transformers, which reduce latency by overlapping loop computation across token positions, but yield rapidly diminishing marginal accuracy gains at larger depths. To address this challenge, we introduce LoopFold, which folds computation at multiple recurrent depths into parallel batches for the same token prefix. A lightweight predictor estimates inputs to later loops so they can start before earlier loops finish. A corrector then refines the outputs of these later loops using newly available results from earlier loops. All components are trained jointly using only the final next-token prediction loss. In experiments with 1.4B models, deeper LoopFold configurations achieve progressively higher average zero-shot accuracy across eight tasks, rising from 53.41% to 56.38%. Vanilla looped models and PLT show limited gains over the same depth range. Compared with a nine-loop vanilla model, LoopFold uses five sequential stages and additional parallel computation to reduce decoding latency by 46%.
original_abstract.source_title: LoopFold: Parallelizing Recurrent Depth in Looped Transformers

en.text: LoopFold reduces sequential dependencies in looped Transformers by predicting inputs to later loops, executing multiple depths in parallel, and correcting their outputs with newly available earlier states. In 1.4B language models, deeper configurations improve average zero-shot accuracy across eight tasks; five sequential stages reduce decoding latency by 46% relative to a nine-loop vanilla model using additional parallel computation. This suggests a latency–compute trade-off for recurrent architectures, with no recommendation evaluation reported.

zh.text: LoopFold 先预测后续循环的输入，让多个深度并行执行，再利用新得到的前序状态修正输出，以减少循环 Transformer 的串行依赖。在 1.4B 语言模型中，更深配置提高了八项任务的平均零样本准确率；相对九次普通循环，五个串行阶段以额外并行计算换取 46% 的解码延迟下降。它提供了循环架构中延迟与计算量的权衡思路，尚未报告推荐实验。

original_abstract.text: Deep click-through rate (CTR) prediction has achieved substantial success through increasingly expressive feature interaction architectures. However, predictive performance also depends on how input-side information is configured before interaction modeling. Existing studies have shown that selecting informative samples, features, or embedding units can improve prediction accuracy. Nevertheless, they primarily optimize these selection mechanisms independently along a single input-side dimension, overlooking their shared basic form and the inherent dependencies across input levels, thereby limiting the effectiveness of input-side dimensional configuration. To address this issue, we propose OptIDC, a unified framework for Optimal Input-side Dimensional Configuration in deep CTR prediction. OptIDC jointly learns sample, feature, and embedding-unit level configurations within a unified framework by integrating their corresponding selection mechanisms. To explicitly coordinate selection decisions across different levels, OptIDC further introduces a selection-weighted Optimal Transport mechanism that aligns coarse- and fine-grained selections via transport over finite measures, thereby alleviating cross-level selection conflicts while preserving the semantics of each input level. Moreover, OptIDC is model-agnostic and can be seamlessly integrated into existing CTR models. Extensive experiments on four real-world benchmark datasets demonstrate that OptIDC consistently achieves higher AUC than existing input-side selection methods, validating the effectiveness of unified input-side dimensional configuration.
original_abstract.source_title: Towards a Unified Framework of Optimal Input-Side Dimensional Configuration for Deep CTR Prediction

en.text: OptIDC jointly learns sample, feature, and embedding-unit selection for deep CTR prediction. Selection-weighted optimal transport coordinates coarse- and fine-grained decisions while retaining the meaning of each input level. The model-agnostic framework reports higher AUC than existing input-side selection methods on four real-world benchmark datasets. It offers a way to coordinate input configuration before feature interaction; the abstract does not establish a scaling law or quantify computational savings.

zh.text: OptIDC 联合学习 CTR 模型的样本、特征和 embedding 单元选择，并通过选择权重参与的最优传输协调不同粒度的决策，减少跨层选择冲突。该框架可接入已有 CTR 模型，作者在四个真实数据基准上报告 AUC 优于现有输入选择方法。可借鉴的是在特征交互前联合配置不同层级的输入；摘要未建立 scaling law，也未量化计算节省。

original_abstract.text:
Variable-length training creates conflicting parallelism requirements across the layers of a hybrid-attention model. The longest samples require wide sequence-parallel (SP) groups of 16 or 32 ranks for full attention, whose cost grows quadratically with sequence length. Sparse-attention layers, dominated by near-linear MoE work, can instead balance most evaluated workloads within node-local SP8 groups. Reusing the wide groups for these layers pushes their all-to-all communication across nodes, where the observed effective rate is 7.0x lower. Yet switching to smaller groups changes which ranks own each sample; a separate redistribution at every full-sparse boundary would introduce another data transfer.
Layerwise Repacking keeps each SP16/32 parent for full attention and repacks its samples into node-local sparse children at SP{1, 2, 4, 8}, where hidden states persist between full layers. The layout change rides on the two existing full-layer Ulysses sites: at each, one variable-size all-to-all performs both the head exchange and the sample repacking, so no redistribution pass is added. Because the balance the children can reach depends on which samples share a parent, an auxiliary parent solver rebalances parent membership before the children are formed.
On all 22 steps with SP16/32 parents among the first 200 training steps of a 1F3S hybrid-attention model (one full-attention layer per three sparse-attention layers), repacking alone reduces the mean end-to-end time by 5.95% and raises model FLOPs utilization (MFU) by 3.75 percentage points over the baseline with repacking disabled; with the improved solver, end-to-end time falls by 7.61% and MFU rises by 4.83 percentage points.
original_abstract.source_title: Layerwise Repacking: Variable-Length Hybrid-Attention Training without an Extra Redistribution Pass

en.text: Layerwise Repacking adapts sequence-parallel groups to variable-length hybrid-attention training: wide groups serve full-attention layers, while node-local child groups serve sparse layers. Sample repacking shares existing Ulysses all-to-all exchanges, avoiding an extra redistribution pass. On the 22 relevant steps among the first 200 steps of a 1F3S model, repacking plus a parent-group solver reduces mean end-to-end time by 7.61% and increases MFU by 4.83 percentage points.

zh.text: Layerwise Repacking 针对变长混合注意力训练，让全注意力层使用较宽的序列并行组，稀疏层使用节点内子组；样本重排复用已有 Ulysses all-to-all 交换，避免额外再分发。在一个 1F3S 模型前 200 步中符合条件的 22 步上，结合父组优化求解器后，平均端到端耗时降低 7.61%，MFU 提高 4.83 个百分点。

original_abstract.text: Sequential recommendation must combine semantic preferences with behavioral associations to deliver accurate rankings at low inference cost. Sharing history selection connects preference representation directly to the behavioral evidence used in candidate scoring. We present RELAY, a compact sequential recommender built around one query, two roles: semantic readout and behavioral-memory routing. A single learned query forms a semantic preference representation and reuses its attention to route direct-history and transition evidence into candidate scores. Candidate-conditioned gates calibrate the two memory channels for each candidate. RELAY trains both roles with a single catalog likelihood and produces the final ranking in one forward pass. Full-catalog experiments on six datasets show that RELAY achieves the highest Recall@5 and NDCG@5 among the compared methods on every dataset, improving over the previous best model by 14.22% and 17.88% on average. With 2.044 million predictor parameters, RELAY reduces predictor size by 65.12% and achieves a 1.75~1.79$\times$ inference speedup over the previous best model.
original_abstract.source_title: RELAY: One Query, Two Roles for Sequential Recommendation

en.text: RELAY reuses one learned query for both semantic preference readout and routing behavioral evidence into candidate scores. Candidate-conditioned gates calibrate direct-history and transition memories, and a single catalog-likelihood objective trains the one-pass ranker. Across six full-catalog benchmarks, it reports average Recall@5 and NDCG@5 improvements of 14.22% and 17.88% over the previous best model. Its 2.044M-parameter predictor is 65.12% smaller and runs 1.75–1.79 times faster than that comparator, illustrating compact history-computation reuse rather than proven industrial scaling.

zh.text: RELAY 复用一个学习得到的查询，既提取语义偏好，也把直接历史和行为转移两类证据送入候选打分，再用候选相关门控调整两类记忆。模型以同一个全目录似然目标训练，一次前向生成排名。在六个全目录评测数据集上，作者报告 Recall@5、NDCG@5 相对此前最佳模型平均提升 14.22%、17.88%。其预测器包含 204.4 万参数，规模减少 65.12%，推理速度为该对照的 1.75–1.79 倍，可供紧凑历史建模参考，尚非工业扩模验证。

original_abstract.text: Sparse expert execution does not remove the stored states needed to adapt a mixture-of-experts language model. We present DuplexTune, a framework for replaying coupled hidden states through pretrained attention and expert modules. Trainable width bridges connect two residual streams to the backbone. Bridge warm-up precedes backbone adaptation, with router weights kept frozen. We analyze the implicit state-recovery equation and identify the convergence and replay conditions needed for reconstruction. On Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B, the single-H800 evaluation reports 38.8 GB peak memory, versus 64.8 GB for supervised fine-tuning with checkpointing, and throughput of 25.1 versus 19.9 samples/s. DuplexTune achieves 67.2% MMLU, 75.6% GSM8K, and 7.69 MT-Bench, with a weaker multilingual score than the checkpointed baseline. The results characterize a configuration-dependent tradeoff among state storage, throughput, and adaptation quality.
original_abstract.source_title: DuplexTune: Coupled-State Replay for Memory-Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Adaptation

en.text: Replays coupled hidden states through pretrained attention and expert modules using trainable width bridges, with bridge warm-up and frozen routers. A single-H800 Qwen1.5-MoE experiment reports 38.8 versus 64.8 GB peak memory and higher throughput than checkpointed fine-tuning, with task-dependent quality tradeoffs including weaker multilingual performance.

zh.text: 以可训练宽度桥连接两条残差流，在预训练注意力和专家模块中重放耦合状态，降低MoE适配时的激活存储。单H800实验的峰值显存由检查点微调的64.8GB降至38.8GB，吞吐提高，但多语言指标较弱，适合借鉴状态重建与质量权衡。

original_abstract.text: Sequential recommendation models typically predict a user's next action from recent session interactions, which limits personalization when short-term signals are weak or ambiguous. Rather than assuming that incorporating longer-term history and community signals is universally beneficial, we study when it actually helps. We propose BehaveRec, a three-signal framework combining a causal session transformer, a bidirectional User History Encoder over a 90-day window, and a GraphSAGE module over a user-user graph built from behavioral embedding similarity rather than item co-occurrence; a learned gate blends the three signals per user. On an industrial dataset of 137M sequences from 12.6M users, BehaveRec improves R@5 by +3.2% over SASRec, with a larger-capacity SASRec baseline (more parameters than BehaveRec) still trailing by +2.5%, ruling out capacity as the explanation. More importantly, a user-level stratification by history length reveals a clear dose-response relationship: BehaveRec's advantage is negligible below roughly 10 interactions and grows monotonically with history richness, reaching +0.017 R@5 for users with 101+ events. This pattern is corroborated across one industrial and three public datasets spanning history-rich to history-sparse regimes, where session-only models remain preferable. These headline results, and the resulting deployment threshold, are established for category-level intent prediction; a preliminary, single-run check on the full item-level vocabulary yields a directionally mixed result and is scoped as an open question rather than a claim. We use these results to derive a practical deployment rule -- roughly 20 interactions per user -- for when long-term history and behavioral-graph signals are worth their added complexity. Despite this added complexity, BehaveRec remains lightweight: it uses 5.67M parameters and trains on a single GPU in under two days.
original_abstract.source_title: BehaveRec: When Does Long-Term Behavioral History Help Sequential Recommendation? A Study with Session, History, and Community Signals

en.text: BehaveRec gates together a causal session transformer, a 90-day history encoder and a behavioral-similarity user graph. On an industrial dataset with 137 million sequences from 12.6 million users, it reports a 3.2% R@5 gain over SASRec, with benefits increasing as histories become richer. Its roughly 20-interaction deployment rule concerns category-level intent prediction; item-level findings are mixed and history-sparse settings may favor session-only models.

zh.text: BehaveRec用门控融合近期会话Transformer、90天历史编码器和基于行为相似性的用户图，研究哪些用户值得加入长历史信号。在覆盖1260万用户、1.37亿序列的工业数据上，论文报告相对SASRec的R@5增幅为3.2%，收益随历史丰富程度增加。约20次交互的部署建议针对类别级意图预测；商品级结果并不一致，历史稀疏时仅用会话可能更合适。

original_abstract.text: Under a fixed embedding-storage budget, recommenders can use a small full-precision model, a distilled student, or a higher-rank low-precision model. We asked which choice preserves rare-item recall and whether teacher fidelity reflects it in seven dataset-backbone cells: matrix factorization on Gowalla, Last.fm, Amazon Video Games, Steam, Goodbooks-10k and MovieLens-20M, and LightGCN on Amazon Video Games. Seven candidates fit in 168 bytes per user or item row: 40-dimensional Bayesian personalized ranking (BPR), two 40-dimensional unbiased knowledge distillation (UnKD) students, and factorizations of a 300-dimensional teacher's scores at ranks 40, 80, 155 and 300, stored in 32, 16, 8 and 4 bits. Each test set was evaluated once after fixing candidates and confirmatory analyses. The rank-300 4-bit factorization used 13% of teacher storage and retained 95-103% of its tail recall@20 and 93-97% of its NDCG@20 in every cell. The rank-40 factorization had the lowest tail recall in every cell; the 4-bit factorization had 1.2-12.7 times its tail recall and 0.99-1.46 times its NDCG. UnKD students retained 56-102% of teacher tail recall. In all ten prespecified comparisons across five prospective-expansion cells, the 4-bit factorization had higher tail recall, with simultaneous 95% intervals excluding zero. Teacher-hit retention, the share of the teacher's relevant tail hits also found by a model, ordered 23 of 147 candidate pairs differently from tail recall and identified the wrong tail-recall leader in 3 of 7 cells: models can find relevant tail items the teacher misses. In these cells, spending bytes on rank rather than precision preserved rare-item recall at 7.5 times the arithmetic per score. Compressed recommenders should be judged by total tail recall, not teacher fidelity alone.
original_abstract.source_title: Preserving rare-item recall under a storage budget: quantization, distillation, and the limits of teacher fidelity

en.text: Under a fixed embedding-storage budget, the study compares low-dimensional models, distilled students and higher-rank low-precision factorizations across seven dataset-backbone cells. A rank-300 4-bit factorization uses 13% of teacher storage while retaining 95–103% of tail recall@20 and 93–97% of NDCG@20, at 7.5 times the arithmetic per score. Teacher-hit retention can misrank candidates, so the authors recommend assessing total rare-item recall directly.

zh.text: 该研究在固定嵌入存储预算下，比较低维模型、蒸馏学生和较高秩低精度分解，覆盖七个数据集—骨干组合。秩 300 的 4 位分解仅使用教师 13% 的存储，保留其 95–103% 的长尾 recall@20 和 93–97% 的 NDCG@20，但每次评分的算术量增加至 7.5 倍。教师命中保留率可能错误排序候选方法，因此作者建议直接评价总的稀有物品召回。

original_abstract.text:
In expert-parallel mixture-of-experts (MoE) serving, dispatch moves tokens to the accelerators hosting their selected experts, and combine returns expert outputs to each token's owner. Both operations lie on the critical path and can dominate MoE layer latency in multi-node deployments. We present INC-MoE, an expert-parallel MoE layer that offloads dispatch and combine to the network switch and overlaps both collectives with each other and with expert computation. Dispatch uses in-network AllGather through switch-side multicast, while combine uses in-network ReduceScatter through switch-side reduction. Both collectives use message semantics between the end hosts and the switch. Because the in-network collectives load opposite directions of each link, executing them concurrently reduces bandwidth-bound communication time by $(N-2)/(2(N-1))$ relative to concurrent ring-based collectives: 33% for four ranks and 43% for eight.
INC-MoE partitions tokens into bands and processes them through a three-stage AllGather-feed-forward network (FFN)-ReduceScatter pipeline inside a single persistent kernel. At steady state, role-specialized thread blocks gather the next band, compute the current band, and reduce the previous band concurrently, overlapping both collectives with each other and with computation using device-side synchronization. INC-MoE integrates as a drop-in replacement for the MoE layer of vLLM. We evaluate it in an emulated four-node scale-out deployment with a dedicated accelerator emulating an in-network computing (INC) switch. On OLMoE prefill with four-way expert parallelism, INC-MoE reduces time to first token (TTFT) by up to 33% and increases throughput by up to 50% relative to vLLM's default collective path, while matching its outputs.
original_abstract.source_title: INC-MoE: Overlapping In-Network Collectives and Expert Computation for Expert-Parallel Mixture-of-Experts Inference

en.text: INC-MoE offloads expert-parallel dispatch and combine to switch-side multicast and reduction, overlapping these collectives with expert computation through a banded persistent-kernel pipeline. It integrates as a vLLM MoE-layer replacement. In an emulated four-node deployment using a dedicated accelerator as the network switch, OLMoE prefill reduces time to first token by up to 33% and raises throughput by up to 50% while matching outputs.

zh.text: INC-MoE 将专家并行的分发与合并卸载到交换机侧的组播和归约，并通过分带持久内核流水线使通信与专家计算重叠，可替换 vLLM 的 MoE 层。在以专用加速器模拟网络交换机的四节点部署中，OLMoE 预填充的首 token 延迟最高降低 33%，吞吐最高提升 50%，同时保持输出一致。

original_abstract.text: For efficiency, industrial large language model (LLM) labelers often pack many candidate labels into one prompt and generate a YES/NO answer for each, even when each decision depends only on the entity and one candidate. Generating these independent decisions as one answer list couples them, spends decoding on the list, and relies on the list being well-formed. In this paper, we present an end-to-end recipe that reformulates the labeler as semantic scoring, fine-tuning it on single-candidate prompts to return each decision as one answer-token score from a prefill-only pass. We also adapt Multiple-Item Scoring (MIS) to score hundreds of candidates in one sequence with attention masked between them. Deployed for profile qualification labeling at LinkedIn, semantic scoring changes at most 0.01% of decisions when candidates are reordered and matches the agreement with reference labels that packed generation reaches only with about 4.7x as many training pairs. The MIS-based stack raises throughput over the deployed stack by 1.24x offline and 1.9x in model serving under a one-second p99 latency target. For offline batch inference, we implement MIS-based scoring as a reusable, model-agnostic Ray Data API proposed for upstream adoption. Model serving uses MIS support contributed to SGLang.
original_abstract.source_title: From Generation to Scoring: Scaling LLM-Based Semantic Labeling at LinkedIn

en.text: LinkedIn replaces packed YES/NO label generation with single-candidate semantic scores from a prefill-only pass, and masks attention between candidates to score hundreds together with Multiple-Item Scoring. Candidate reordering changes at most 0.01% of decisions. Compared with the deployed stack, throughput rises 1.24x offline and 1.9x in serving under a one-second p99 target. The application is profile qualification labeling, not an online CTR gain.

zh.text: LinkedIn将一串YES/NO标签的生成改成单候选语义打分，只做预填充，并通过候选间注意力隔离在一个序列里同时评估数百候选。候选重排最多改变0.01%的决策；相对原部署栈，离线吞吐为1.24倍，在p99一秒目标下在线吞吐为1.9倍。实验用于个人资料资质标签生成，不应解读为线上CTR提升。

original_abstract.text: Daily item co-occurrence embeddings are paired with next-day behavior without future-behavior leakage. Multi-day click-through rate (CTR) training therefore mixes versions whose directions and norms may differ for the same item. We compare Word2Vec and an item-graph XSimGCL adaptation across initialization, inheritance, post-processing, training constraints, and downstream augmentation. The inventory contains 48 configurations, including 32 common-protocol CTR evaluations. Observed metrics are reported as relative percentage changes from the corresponding Word2Vec baseline (0%), with raw values and exact dataset sizes withheld. Three findings emerge. First, multiple upstream interventions improve compatibility and CTR. ID-init and orthogonal alignment increase cosine by 51.2% and 93.4%, and GAUC by 2.2% and 2.6%, relative to ordinary Word2Vec. Retrieval and geometry remain insufficient downstream surrogates. Second, warm starts perform strongly but accumulate scale. The day-matched norm increase over Word2Vec reaches 102.5% after eight days; daily global rescaling limits it to 8.2% and attains the highest observed GAUC increase, 4.0%. Third, CTR learning through a dimensionality-reducing encoder further adapts to residual drift. Against dimension-matched random-projection, SVD, and untrained-network controls, trained encoders attain the highest cross-day cosine for four of six upstream methods. The other two rank third and second in train-to-test cosine. These industrial results support complementary roles for upstream stabilization, inherited-scale management, and downstream task learning.
original_abstract.source_title: Cross-Day Compatibility of Daily Item Embeddings: An Empirical Study of Alignment, Scale Management, and CTR Adaptation

en.text: This empirical study examines daily item-embedding drift in multi-day CTR training through 48 configurations, including 32 common-protocol CTR evaluations. Alignment, warm-start scale control and downstream encoders play complementary roles. Daily global rescaling achieves the highest observed GAUC gain of 4.0% relative to the corresponding Word2Vec baseline. Raw metric values and exact dataset sizes are withheld, and better retrieval or geometric compatibility does not necessarily imply better CTR.

zh.text: 该研究分析每天更新的商品embedding在跨日CTR训练中出现的方向与尺度漂移，比较48种配置，其中32种进行了统一协议CTR评测。对齐、热启动后的尺度控制和下游编码器各有作用；每日全局重缩放取得所测最高GAUC相对增幅4.0%，基线为对应Word2Vec配置。论文未公开原始指标与精确数据规模，检索或几何相容性改善也不必然对应CTR收益。

original_abstract.text: Attention Matching (AM) compacts a KV cache by keeping some keys per head, refitting their values and adding a bias to each kept key's logit. FlashAttention and vLLM's paged caches have no input for it. We fold the bias into the keys along one closed-form direction per head, fitted on context queries, giving a plain cache with AM's size and head dimension and the model's own query path; the output error is bounded by how far each query's projection on that direction is from 1. With equal per-head budgets, unmodified vLLM serves folded caches through a KV connector, matching Hugging Face's answers on all 51 Qwen3-4B questions and its greedy output on 180 of 200 Qwen3-14B LongBench samples. With equal budgets on QuALITY (Qwen3-1.7B, 4B, 8B, Llama-3.1-8B) and LongHealth (three Qwen3 models), the fold is within noise of AM's accuracy in 13 of 14 settings, with lower KL to the full cache than dropping the bias in all 12 where both ran. Under the published per-head budgets, on Qwen3-4B, its Instruct-2507 variant and Llama-3.1-8B, it is within noise of AM in 9 of 10, no longer beats dropping the bias in KL, and the two each win once in accuracy.
original_abstract.source_title: Folding Attention Biases into Keys Makes Compacted KV Caches Run on Standard Kernels

en.text: The method folds Attention Matching logit biases into retained keys along one fitted direction per head, producing compact KV caches compatible with standard attention kernels and the original query path. Unmodified vLLM serves these caches through a connector. Under equal head budgets, accuracy is within noise of Attention Matching in 13 of 14 tested settings; results are less uniformly favorable under the published per-head budgets, emphasizing budget-dependent tradeoffs.

zh.text: 该方法沿每个注意力头拟合的一条方向，将 Attention Matching 的 logit 偏置折叠到保留的键中，得到兼容标准注意力内核及原查询路径的压缩 KV 缓存，可经连接器由未修改的 vLLM 服务。在各头预算相同的测试中，14 个设定有 13 个准确率与 Attention Matching 的差异处于噪声范围；采用其公开的逐头预算时优势不再一致，说明效果依赖预算配置。

original_abstract.text: Mamba-2 compresses all context into a fixed-size recurrent state that dominates decoding memory and bandwidth. Existing compressors quantize state values or prune state coordinates, scoring each channel independently in the native basis. We examine trained Mamba-2 states and find that energy is almost rank-one, but the output does not read the energetic directions: energy concentrates in a bias-like direction accumulated by the recurrence, while the content the output reads lives in a low-dimensional subspace that is not aligned with the state's coordinates. Even output-aware scores are computed coordinate by coordinate, so they miss the directions that determine the input--output map. Compression should therefore target the write--read subspace rather than individual coordinates. We propose \method{}, a post-training transform that instantiates balanced truncation with full controllability and observability Gramians and applies the rotation exactly via Mamba-2's scalar-identity transition. Because the useful rank varies widely across layers, we further introduce HARP, which allocates ranks per layer from the Hankel spectrum and protects retrieval-sensitive layers, improving both perplexity and retrieval over uniform budgets. Calibration takes a single forward pass, an order of magnitude faster than GHOST's released protocol, with lower peak memory. With HARP, \method{} halves the state dimension at an average WikiText-2 perplexity increase of $0.3$ points ($1.8\%$) across 130M--2.7B, versus $1.6$ ($9.3\%$) for GHOST, and the gap widens at 25\% retention.
original_abstract.source_title: Balanced State Subspaces for Mamba-2 State Compression

en.text: This method compresses Mamba-2 states by targeting the subspace connecting state writes to output reads, rather than pruning coordinates independently. A post-training balanced-truncation transform rotates that subspace, while HARP allocates ranks across layers and protects retrieval-sensitive layers. One-forward-pass calibration is reported to be an order of magnitude faster than GHOST's released protocol; across 130M–2.7B models, halving state dimension raises average WikiText-2 perplexity by 0.3 points versus 1.6 for GHOST. It offers a state-compression design for long-history models, not demonstrated CTR gains.

zh.text: 这项方法压缩 Mamba-2 的循环状态时，保留连接写入与输出读取的低维子空间，而非逐坐标独立裁剪。训练后的平衡截断变换旋转状态空间，HARP 再按层分配保留维度，并保护对检索敏感的层。校准只需一次前向计算，摘要报告比 GHOST 公布的流程快一个数量级；在 1.3 亿至 27 亿参数模型上，状态维度减半后，WikiText-2 平均困惑度增加 0.3，GHOST 为 1.6。可借鉴的是长历史模型的状态压缩设计，尚无 CTR 效果验证。

original_abstract.text: Generative recommendation (GR) predicts the next item through its semantic ID (SID). Existing methods commonly fit SID vocabularies to pretrained language model (PLM) representations of item descriptions, incurring additional training costs and making vocabulary coverage dependent on the fitting domains. We observe that pretrained sparse autoencoders expose PLM features with human-interpretable semantic annotations, allowing feature indices to serve as a reusable SID vocabulary. However, reusing this vocabulary requires preserving item distinctions under compact token budgets and learning to favor target items over candidates with shared dominant features. It also requires extending feature interpretability from item content to retrieval decisions. To address these challenges, we propose API, a framework that Adapts the Pretrained Interpretable vocabulary for effective and explainable GR without additional vocabulary learning. Within API, Pretrained Interpretable IDs (PIDs) retain selected feature indices and relative activation strengths for item discrimination. With PIDs as supervision, the Semantic Prediction Adapter (SPA) learns user preferences from interaction histories through joint feature-index and strength prediction. SPA combines both predictions to score candidate items, with item-level supervision encouraging the observed next item to outrank its alternatives. API further explains candidate score differences through feature contributions paired with their pretrained semantic annotations. Extensive experiments show that API achieves competitive performance across backbones and decoding schemes, while preserving item distinctions under compact token budgets and enabling explainable retrieval.
original_abstract.source_title: The Vocabulary Is Already Here: Adapting Pretrained Interpretable Features for Generative Recommendation

en.text: API reuses interpretable features from pretrained sparse autoencoders as a semantic-ID vocabulary without training a new vocabulary. Its IDs retain feature indices and relative strengths; a semantic prediction adapter jointly predicts both to score items from user histories. Feature contributions explain candidate-score differences. Experiments report competitive recommendation across backbones and decoding schemes while preserving item distinctions under compact token budgets.

zh.text: API 复用预训练稀疏自编码器的可解释特征作为语义 ID 词表，无需重新训练词表。其 ID 保留特征索引和相对激活强度，语义预测适配器根据用户历史联合预测二者并给候选评分，以特征贡献解释分数差异。实验报告在不同骨干和解码方式下具有竞争力，并能在紧凑 token 预算内保留物品差异。

original_abstract.text: Quadratic approximations provide a common lens for studying neural network optimization, but recent evidence challenges their predictive validity. In full-batch gradient descent with learning rate (LR) $\eta$, Cohen et al. (2021) observed the Edge of Stability (EoS), where the largest Hessian eigenvalue concentrates near $2/\eta$, seemingly at odds with classical stability conditions predicted by quadratic approximations. In this work, we revisit the fidelity of quadratic approximations as a model of neural network training dynamics, with a particular focus on their failure modes in LLM training. We first highlight a distinct failure mode of the quadratic approximation, where persistent negative curvature causes the quadratic dynamics to diverge regardless of the LR, even though the real dynamics remain stable. We term this phenomenon the Edge of Convexity (EoC). After removing the effect of this LR-independent instability, we then propose a generalized definition of Edge of Stability (EoS) for stochastic training with adaptive optimizers, based on whether increasing the LR induces significant divergence in the quadratic dynamics while leaving the real dynamics largely unchanged. Across different LLM pretraining runs with various model sizes up to 787M, we find that (1) EoC is always observed across LLM pretraining, and (2) EoS is also prevalent but not universal: it disappears when the LR becomes sufficiently small (e.g., after decay) or when the batch size falls below a critical threshold that has a positive correlation with the critical batch size. Together, these findings characterize when and how quadratic approximations fail and provide a foundation for future work on understanding training dynamics.
original_abstract.source_title: Does LLM Pre-Training Typically Occur at the Edge of Stability?

en.text: This study tests when quadratic approximations misrepresent language-model training dynamics. Persistent negative curvature can make the approximate dynamics diverge at any learning rate while real training remains stable; after separating that effect, the authors define a stability-edge diagnostic for stochastic adaptive optimization. In pretraining runs up to 787M parameters, the learning-rate-dependent effect is common but disappears at sufficiently small learning rates or batch sizes. The results caution against equating local curvature-based instability with failed training; they do not provide a new optimizer or CTR evidence.

zh.text: 这项研究检验二次近似何时无法描述语言模型训练：持续的负曲率可能让近似动力学在任意学习率下都发散，而真实训练仍然稳定。分离这一影响后，作者提出适用于随机自适应优化的稳定性边缘诊断。在最大 7.87 亿参数的预训练实验中，与学习率相关的这种现象较常见，但学习率或批量足够小时会消失。可借鉴的是判断训练稳定性时，不把局部曲率近似的发散直接视为训练失败；论文未提出新优化器或验证 CTR 效果。

original_abstract.text: Generative recommendation (GR) models for ranking typically adopt a fast-thinking direct prediction paradigm with strong practical efficiency. However, ranking requires fine-grained scoring across multiple candidate items, while existing GR models still mainly rely on one-shot prediction. This raises the question whether additional inference-time computation can further improve ranking quality. Recently, inspired by Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning in large language models (LLMs), some work has begun to introduce reasoning into recommendation systems. Some of these methods rely on LLM reasoning frameworks to perform explicit reasoning in textual space, but such designs are not suitable for more widely deployed non-textual recommendation models. A more relevant direction is to introduce latent reasoning into ID-based recommendation models. Although recent work has extended latent reasoning to industrial ranking, how successive reasoning steps should improve fine-grained candidate scores remains less explored. To address this problem, we propose Refiner, a latent residual reasoning framework with parameter-efficient fine-tuning for generative ranking. Our approach introduces three key components: (1) a residual reasoning mechanism that progressively refines ranking scores through cumulative additive corrections, (2) history queries that provide condensed user behavior representations to enhance candidate-specific reasoning, and (3) a parameter-efficient fine-tuning strategy that leverages LoRA modules to adapt pre-trained models for latent reasoning. Extensive experiments on two public benchmarks, an offline industrial dataset, and an online A/B test demonstrate that Refiner consistently improves over direct prediction, validating its effectiveness and practical utility.
original_abstract.source_title: Latent Residual Reasoning for Ranking in Generative Recommendation

en.text: Refiner adds latent residual reasoning to generative ranking: successive steps make additive corrections to candidate scores, guided by condensed history queries. LoRA adapts pretrained models with parameter-efficient fine-tuning. Experiments on two public benchmarks, an industrial dataset and an online A/B test report consistent gains over direct prediction, supporting additional inference-time computation for ranking.

zh.text: Refiner 为生成式排序引入潜在残差推理：利用压缩的历史查询引导候选级推理，通过连续的加性修正逐步改进分数，并以 LoRA 对预训练模型进行参数高效微调。两个公开基准、工业数据集及线上 A/B 测试均报告优于直接预测的结果，支持通过增加推理时计算改善排序。
